what_it_does: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is a technique that lets a server do calculations on encrypted data without ever decrypting it — so a cloud provider could run AI models on your private medical records without ever seeing the records. The catch is that FHE is enormously slow, sometimes millions of times slower than working with plain numbers. Custom chips built for FHE are fast but quickly become obsolete as FHE algorithms evolve. Neo instead runs FHE on ordinary GPU hardware by rewriting the dominant FHE operations — particularly a step called Number Theoretic Transform (NTT), which is a fast way of multiplying large polynomials, i.e., doing the core math of FHE — as large matrix multiplications that fit directly onto the GPU's built-in matrix-math units (called Tensor Cores, which are specialized circuits that multiply and add arrays of numbers very quickly in INT8 or FP16 low-precision arithmetic). Careful bookkeeping ensures the low-precision arithmetic does not introduce errors that would corrupt the encryption.
